finding: Five card_catalog rows address a 2022 Topps Chrome image variation at card #221. No such card exists. rulings: R64 (Drew, 2026-09-18): Witt #221 pooled four different cards; split them. R64's chosen Refractor destination was `image-variation-refractor`, an ingest-auto-seed row.

R64b (2026-09-18): the pricing engine WITHHELD on that destination - 'no-checklist-match ... identitySource ingest-auto-seed, backing self-derived-only' - and it was right. Cardboard Connection: the base set is '220 cards numbered 1-220' and 221-225 are 'not part of the main base set' but the 'Extended Base Short Prints' subset ('Card 221: Bobby Witt Jr.'). checklistcenter: an 'Extended Base SP Set (5 cards: #221-225)' SEPARATE from a 'Base Image Variation Set (20 cards)' running 1..220, and Witt #221 'appears only in the Extended Base SP Set, not in the Image Variations section (which tops out at #220)'. The sales now live on the checklist-backed `:221:refractor:` and `:221:base:` rows, and the holding prices $253.95 there.

cardpedia-drew-ruling-2026-09-11 (Ruling 23) is CITED AND REVERSED for this card: it minted `image-variation-sonic` from BCP's Gimmicks line on the reading that #221's variation is Sonic. R64 withdrew that premise; R64b showed the Sonic image variations are the SONIC LITE product's, and their 6 sales sit on that product's own checklistcenter-backed row.

RETIRE IS A HARD DELETE in this lane (retireCatalogRow: graded children, then the row) and it re-points NOTHING. That is safe here and only here because every id below point-reads 0 sales and 0 holdings - verified 2026-09-18, and stated per row in its evidence. If any had sales, the entry would be listed BLOCKED rather than retired.

NOT IN THIS LIST, deliberately: `hiq:baseball:2022:topps-chrome-sonic-lite:221:image-variations:no-auto`. It is checklistcenter-backed, it is the real Sonic Lite image variation, and it holds the 6 Sonic sales. Retiring it would delete a real card and unplace live sales.
The graded children are NAMED rather than left to the lane's own child sweep, so the operator can see every id this list deletes before the apply.

A RETIRE LIST MUST COUNT BY BOTH IDENTITY FIELDS, and this list is the proof. It originally carried 5 entries. The lane's own REPORT disagreed with my point-read - 'sales pointing here: 2' where a cardId query said 0 - because the lane counts by hobbyiqCardId (that is what retireCatalogRow leaves behind) while CardHedge rows are partitioned on the CH product id. A paged fetchNext read compounded it, returning 0 for a row that has 2. The row is now BLOCKED, the two sales are named, and the remaining four are verified 0/0 by cardId AND hobbyiqCardId with fetchAll.
